newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO AND BETIS WIN AWAY TO KEEP UP PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO AND BETIS WIN AWAY TO KEEP UP PRESSURE.

text.p: A solitary goal from Frenchman Corentin Martins ensured Deportivo Coruna three points from their game at Sevilla on Sunday and with it second place in the Spanish first division behind leaders Real Madrid.
With 33 points from 15 games, Deportivo are two off the pace after Real's 1-0 win at Sporting Gijon on Saturday, and two ahead of Barcelona, who play Extremadura on Monday.
Martins pounced on a rebound early in the second half of a poor game which ended with Sevilla fans shouting insults at the club president's box.

"The fans don't have confidence in the team...something's lacking," said Sevilla coach Jose Antonio Camacho, who offered his resignation after the game only to see the club board offer him their full support.
Camacho, who took Espanyol to a UEFA Cup place last season, has lost three consecutive games and his team has dropped to fourth from bottom.

By contrast Sevilla's local rivals Real Betis are going from strength to strength. Betis defended well at Compostela to run out 2-0 winners with goals from Alfonso Perez and Nigerian international Finidi George.
With 29 points Betis hold fourth place, two points ahead of reigning champions Atletico Madrid, who beat Racing Santander 1-0 on Saturday.
A further two points back in sixth are Athletic Bilbao, who lost ground with the goalless draw at Valalladolid.
Struggling Zaragoza were able to dedicate their first home win of the season -- 1-0 over Oviedo -- to late club president Alfonso Solans, who died on Friday morning.
Solans was remembered with a minute of silence in all Spanish first division games played over the weekend.
